While I have always found the staff to be lovely, we have been disappointed with our recent experiences over the last few months in how our cat has been treated. Our male cat blocked and required in and out catheterisation to drain his bladder. Grit was found but was quickly dismissed when his test results came back as clear. As such it was put down to stress.

Less than three months later he reblocked again, his bladder was partially full but he was unable to pass urine when the vet tried to express it. He was given pain relief and medication to take home, by 4am he still hadn’t peed so we called VetsNow as it wasn’t made clear to us how long we should wait until the medication kicked in and we were worried his condition would develop into an emergency.

As your out of hours service I would have expected them to have access to his notes but this did not seem to be the case. As such, he went through the procedure again without any background context aside from what we could remember. Like your team, they found grit when trying to unblock him but did not investigate any further. As the root cause of the issue was not identified, he reblocked for a third time but was in a significantly worse condition as he’d just been through stressful surgery.

We made the decision to move him to Rouken Glen vets and we are so glad that we did - he was flushed out multiple times until the vet could find the crystals causing the grit. He was kept in over night and observed until he was peeing multiple times. It turns out he had urate crystals which would not show up in the standard tests but as grit was present, the vet at Rouken Glen refused to empty his bladder and send him home until this cause of it was identified as he would just continue to reblock.

Had Roundhouse properly looked into the cause of the grit they found in the first place then our cat wouldn’t have reblocked twice (something which has been extremely traumatic for him), he would be on the correct aftercare and diet which would manage his condition and we’d be nearly £3.5k better off.

For comparison on costs, Roundhouse charged £1.2k for the initial unblocking  treatment, VetsNow charged £2.7k and Rouken Glen who kept him in for two full days, undertook an unblocking, numerous flushes and identified the root cause, charged £625.

The quality of aftercare is also significantly better at Rouken Glen than at both Roundhouse and VetsNow with our cat receiving injectables which will last him weeks vs the need for multiple pills and liquid medication to be administered throughout the day for weeks. The vet at RG also took the time to walk us through everything in detail and made us feel reassured that he was finally in the right hands.

Great with my very nervous dog and so patient with my multiple calls during his surgery.
Staff are lovely, the environment is clean and you can tell they just love on your pets like their own 🥰 …

Seemed like a decently nice vet at the beginning but after experiences alongside preexisting reviews from other people, this place will bleed you dry or be incredibly dishonest. I took my cat in for a neutering at 7 months and a few hours after the surgery had taken place I called and asked for an update on her status. They claimed she was fine, no issues at all, and she was ready to be picked up in 30 minutes. Once I picked her up I saw that there was an additional £70-£80 bill on top of the £100 deposit and £109 final payment; this was for eye ulcer medication which nobody informed me about until 20 minutes after I had came in and checked with reception. The part I disagree with is the vet telling me this was a very common risk of neutering under anaesthesia for cats, which I then later found from other vets and online forums is not true and eye ulcers are much rarer side effects, often resulting from careless inattentiveness from the vets when they meant to be lubricating the cat’s eyes during surgery. Ridiculous prices for the surgery which you can’t really even seem to find online anywhere, and the medication being brought up on a whim for x3 the price you can get it for elsewhere is a joke. Granted, there are some nice friendly staff but don’t let that fool you.

Some of the vets that work at the roundhouse are extremely good, but like all workplaces, there are exceptions.

Last month, my cat Jack was put to sleep due to a blocked bladder.  I was warned before I had gone to this hospital that they are ultra busy due to the lockdown and resources were scarce. I rushed my cat to this hospital as soon as I could thinking they could unblock the cat and also perform surgery to avoid this happening again, which I was happy to pay for.

The following morning, I got a call at 5am from a vet (I can't remember the name, just the Irish accent) informing me that they could not install a catheter due to spasms. This was followed by a barrage of sighing and when we went through the options, he pretty much put an extremely negative slant on them all, maneuvering me into accepting he had to be euthanized. This may have been unavoidable and I would like to think that was the case, but after getting a second opinion from another vet, she has asked why the hospital did not administer an anti spasm medication when installing the catheter failed the first time. I requested an investigation from the hospital last month. It is now the 4th of October and I have had no communication from them.

The other issue that bothered me was that after agreeing to put Jack down, they could see myself and my wife were both very upset. Rather than give us a day to greave or even half a day, I got a call 2 hours later asking for my card number to pay for Jacks treatment and also for the cremation services. I guess vets are used to putting down animals, but I would expect some empathy from them, I mean, what's a day to them?

I still believe if I had taken Jack to the Garscube vet hospital, he would still be alive today and would have been given the medication to relax his spasms, but it's too late now. If you find yourself in a similar position and and advised to put your pet down, consider getting a second opinion even more so if you are warned they may be too busy to do anything due to the lockdown. If someone tells you that, they should really be advising you try somewhere else rather than play Russian roulette with your pets life and your wallet.

I got a 7 month old rescue dog who didn’t pee when I took her out. I went to the Roundhouse vet who examined her thoroughly and told me her bladder was full and she would need an operation to empty her bladder and it was at dangerous levels and it would require an anaesthetic and an overnight stay. It would cost £2500. I decided to go and have a think about it.

I then decided to get a second opinion. I went to my old vet and they also examined her. They said her bladder was fine and that she was definitely peeing somewhere and that I should go back and check my house. I did and discovered she had been peeing in a back room on some rugs. What’s that all about Roundhouse vets??? Dodged a bullet there I think.

only 1 star so i could post this,will drain all the money they can from you. one time i was in,a woman who hadnt seen my dog before told me that the best thing to do was put her down(she had a leg infection which was swelling up),i told her no chance and the woman told me if i left she would call the police,to which i told her you will need more than that to stop me leaving here with my dog,I want to speak to your superior right now. he came in,had a quick look,my wee dog was happy to see him for a clap,she jumped up onto the 4 foot high table when he tapped it when i thought id have to lift her,and then a minute later turned to the woman and said "shes lively,happy and healthy apart from the leg,why did you say to this guy she needed to be put to sleep?". I laughed at her in a very sarcastically but angry way,and called her what she was...dont use this practice,you will be bled dry in bills, and thats if you dont get coerced into euthanising your pet first.

I was so upset because they basically said to me if my dog was bleeding internally on a table they wouldn’t treat him, my dogs are like my kids & I love them so dearly, so to speak about my dog in that manner was horrific & very upsetting. I was told I’d also be charged £82 for this test, I feel really upset & angry by this. I have been a loyal & faithful customer of theirs these past few years & I have been so badly let down by this experience, it was horrible.

The so called lead vet called back when I got home as I called up really upset, I found her manner very condescending & abrupt.

I would now not recommend this practice whatsoever which is a shame as I thought they had heart until today. Do yourself a favour take your money elsewhere to a practice that actually values you & your animals.

Badly done dental surgery, and poor aftercare. £1600 spent, dog left with inadequate pain relief and an infection. Second opinion was needed.

My dog has been a patient at this practice for 4 years, and we've never had any issues until now. In August 2024, my dog went in for a routine dental to have some teeth removed. They only took one out before stopping the surgery because she was bleeding too much. They should have prescribed her blood clotting medication before the surgery (she is a greyhound and excess bleeding is a well-known issue with the breed) but they didn't. So, one tooth out and £600 spent.

December 2024, she went in for her Stage 2 dental to get the remaining teeth removed (£810). This time, they gave her the blood clotting medication beforehand and the surgery went well. She had 9 teeth removed in total (more than they had told me she needed) and they sent her home with Metacam, once a day. I trusted that this would be adequate pain relief. Two days later, I woke up to my dog crying in pain, bed and face covered in blood, having burst stitches during the night. They then gave me better pain relief (£35) and then extended it a few days later (£25).

Looking at my dog's mouth I could see stitches (different types, too, dissolving and regular) and a large cavity that was irritated and looked infected (pictured). I took her to another vet for a second opinion and was advised that stitches should not have been used at all as they increase risk of infection (duh?) and that she did indeed have a nasty infection in her mouth. She was prescribed antibiotics and further pain relief (£120).

So, I am now £1600 down, with a dog who has been in intense and unnecessary pain for the past ten days, and a vet who did nothing but shrug at me when I expressed I wasn't happy with the care provided. I will be submitting a formal complaint and won't be back.
